A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the finiteness of QFTs can be understood in terms of an underlying theory.
the finiteness following from underlying theory (FFUT) is a natural strategy for getting rid of the unphysical UV divergences in a QFT.
the renormalization programs are not necessary for the UV finiteness of QFTs if the underlying theory is well-defined.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the UV divergences are not an inherent feature of a QFT, but rather an indication of a missing piece in our understanding of the fundamental theory that underlies it.
the finiteness of a QFT is an intrinsic property of the underlying fundamental theory.
the UV divergence is an intrinsic feature of the underlying theory, and the renormalization program is a necessary and sufficient condition for the underlying theory to manifest itself.
